definitions.explanation: A large piece of cloth or fabric stretched horizontally, typically bearing a message, slogan, or design. Used at sporting events, demonstrations, ceremonies, and other gatherings.

examples.japanese: {横断幕|おうだんまく}を{掲|かか}げる。
スタジアムに{応援|おうえん}の{横断幕|おうだんまく}が{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: Cheering banners were lined up at the stadium.

examples.japanese: デモの{参加者|さんかしゃ}たちは「{戦争|せんそう}{反対|はんたい}」と{書|か}かれた{横断幕|おうだんまく}を{持|も}って{行進|こうしん}した。
examples.english: The demonstrators marched carrying banners that read "No War."

notes:
Composed of {横断|おうだん} (crossing horizontally) and {幕|まく} (curtain/screen). The name describes the horizontal orientation of the banner, distinguishing it from vertical banners ({垂|た}れ{幕|まく}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {横断幕|おうだんまく}を{掲|かか}げる: to hold up / display a banner
- {横断幕|おうだんまく}を{張|は}る: to stretch out a banner
- {応援|おうえん}{横断幕|おうだんまく}: cheering banner
- {抗議|こうぎ}の{横断幕|おうだんまく}: protest banner
- {横断幕|おうだんまく}に{書|か}く: to write on a banner

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {垂|た}れ{幕|まく}: vertical banner / hanging banner — hangs vertically rather than stretching horizontally
- {旗|はた}: flag — a piece of cloth attached to a pole, not stretched between two points
- {幕|まく}: curtain / screen — broader term for any large piece of fabric used as a screen
- のぼり: vertical flag / streamer — a tall, narrow flag on a pole, common at shops and events
